---
title: Mastermind store Worker
description: The Cloudflare Durable Object that holds the live fleet snapshot, owner answers and Mastermind push-event claims, with its billing bounds, stop fence and deployment steps.
updatedAt: "2026-11-20"
---

`apps/mastermind-store` is a Cloudflare Worker in front of one SQLite Durable
Object (`MastermindStore`). Web's Mastermind routes use it as their only
state store: the [fleet sync](/platform/features/mobile-mastermind#fleet-sync)
snapshot, owner answers and pickups, publisher nonces, and the
`/api/v1/mastermind/push-events` replay and coalescing claims.

## Why these Cloudflare services

| Service | Use | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Durable Object (SQLite) | All state | One writer with strong consistency: compare-and-set answer revisions, once-only nonces and claims, TTLs. |
| Cache API | The polled snapshot read | A `get` with `cacheMs` (at most 5 s) is answered from the per-colo cache, so several polling clients cost one object read per colo per window. |
| Analytics Engine | Health metrics | One data point per request (route, op kinds, status, latency); never keys or values. Optional binding. |
| Bearer service token | Web to Worker | One caller; constant-time comparison against a rotation list. Cloudflare Access would add an application and a header pair without a gain for a single caller. |

Not used yet: Queues (the publisher re-sends every 30 s, answers are pulled
and acknowledged, and push delivery stays in Web), R2 (nothing references
large artifacts from fleet state yet) and KV (the Cache API covers read
fan-out without KV's eventual consistency or per-write cost).

## Protocol

`packages/utils/src/mastermind-store/protocol.ts` defines `POST /v1/ops` with
1 to 8 ops per request: `get` (optional `cacheMs`), `mget` (up to 64 keys),
`set` (`always` or `nx`), `cas` (compare-and-set; `expect: null` means
absent), `cad` (compare-and-delete) and `del`. A request runs in one
transaction: every op or none. `client.ts` is the typed client (one attempt,
four-second timeout, no redirects) and an in-memory reference store with the
same semantics for tests.

Operator routes use a separate token: `GET /v1/status` (fence, today's
writes, budget, live rows) and `POST /v1/fence` with `{"stopped": true}` or
`false`. Any other path answers 404.

## Billing bounds and stop fence

- No alarms, crons, queues, self-scheduling or retries inside the Worker.
- At most 8 ops per request, a 320 KiB body, 300 KiB per value and 160
  characters per key; at most 5,000 live rows (a write that would add one
  more fails the batch with `full`, 507).
- Writes per UTC day are charged durably in the object before they run and
  refused past `MASTERMIND_STORE_DAILY_WRITE_BUDGET` (default 50,000) with
  `budget` (429). A refused batch charges nothing. Reads are not charged.
- Expired rows are deleted at most 20 per write batch, never in a sweep.
- The stop fence is stored in the object, survives restarts and refuses every
  op with `stopped` (503) until the operator clears it. Service tokens cannot
  change it.

Cost envelope at normal load: the publisher writes once on change and at
least every two minutes (at most 2,880 state writes plus one nonce write
each, about 6,000 rows a day), owner answers add a handful, and push events
add four to six writes per delivered event. Snapshot polls (one owner, every
15 s while a screen is open) are mostly Cache API hits. The daily budget caps
the failure case at 50,000 row writes, well inside the Workers Paid
allowance. Billed usage is verified from the account after publication.

Regressions: `apps/mastermind-store/src/engine.test.ts` (budget charging and
rollover, refused batches charge nothing, the row cap rolls the batch back,
bounded cleanup, the fence) and `src/worker.test.ts` (the emitted Worker in
workerd: auth and rotation, oversize and bad ops, the budget, the fence across
a restart, cached reads).

## Web configuration

| Variable | Where | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MASTERMIND_STORE_URL` | Web | HTTPS origin of the Worker's custom hostname. |
| `MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKEN` | Web | One of the Worker's service tokens (at least 32 characters). |
| `MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKENS` | Worker secret | Comma-separated service tokens; two during rotation. |
| `MASTERMIND_STORE_OPERATOR_TOKEN` | Worker secret | Fence and status only. |
| `MASTERMIND_STORE_DAILY_WRITE_BUDGET` | Worker text | Daily write cap; invalid values make every call answer 503. |

Without `MASTERMIND_STORE_URL` and `MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKEN`, Web falls back to
a legacy Upstash REST client when one is configured, and otherwise answers 503
on the fleet and push-event routes. The resolution lives in
`apps/web/src/lib/mastermind/store.ts`.

## Publication

The `Mastermind Store Cloudflare Artifact` workflow runs on `main` changes to
the Worker or its protocol: tests, type check, lint, format, `vp build`, a
publication-shape assertion (`workersDev` and preview URLs off, SQLite
export, both tokens as secrets) and a reproducible tar of
`.cloudflare/output/v0` with its SHA-256 digest. It deploys nothing.

To publish:

1. Download the artifact for the exact commit and verify its digest.
2. Create the Analytics Engine dataset binding target if the account lacks it.
3. Set `MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKENS` and `MASTERMIND_STORE_OPERATOR_TOKEN` as
   Worker secrets (generated, never printed), then `cf deploy --prebuilt`.
4. Attach the custom hostname; keep `workers.dev` and previews off.
5. Smoke: `GET /v1/status` with the operator token answers `ok: true`, an
   unauthenticated `POST /v1/ops` answers 401, then set and clear the fence
   once.
6. Set `MASTERMIND_STORE_URL` and `MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKEN` on Web production
   and deploy Web; the fleet publisher's next run should log `published`.

Rollback: remove `MASTERMIND_STORE_URL` from Web (the routes answer 503
again) or set the fence. Deleting the Worker loses the snapshot and pending
answers; the publisher re-sends the snapshot within two minutes, and answers
not yet picked up must be given again.
